mainTopic: Late קרבנות, the uses of ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״, and the משנה on mixing place-thoughts and time-thoughts in פיגול.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the defense of בן עזאי's פסוק, which teaches that a קרבן brought late still works. A ברייתא learns from a היקש to מעשר that a late בכור is not פסול, but a בכור does not bring הרצאה, so other קרבנות still need a source. ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ cannot serve as that source, because it teaches that the sin of בל תאחר falls on the man and not on his wife. The גמרא then asks what רבי אליעזר learns from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״. The answer is רבי ינאי's teaching that mixed thoughts cancel פיגול. In רב מרי's version, the teaching is instead that a wrong thought brings מלקות, which follows רבי יהודה. A new משנה follows: a place-thought makes a קרבן פסול, while a time-thought makes it פיגול with כרת, but only if the מתיר was offered כמצותו. רבי יהודה says the thought that came first decides, and חכמים say mixed thoughts are always just פסול. The גמרא brings אילפא and רבי יוחנן arguing whether this dispute applies within one service, and begins to challenge רבי יוחנן from the structure of the משנה.

steps.title: The ברייתא wonders if a late firstborn becomes disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the idea that a בכור kept past its year should be treated like other disqualified קדשים and be פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it should be like disqualified consecrated animals, and be disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that the גמרא is quoting. The ברייתא raises a possible thought: a בכור that passed its year might become פסול, and it sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is supposed to be given to the כהן within its first year. The ברייתא wonders whether missing that deadline ruins the animal, the way a מום ruins a קרבן. This is the starting thought that the ברייתא is about to reject.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became disqualified from being offered
And it should be disqualified

phrases.english: like disqualified consecrated animals, and it should be disqualified?
phrases.notes: This is still the ברייתא talking about a בכור whose first year has passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting before this section to challenge בן עזאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a בכור become פסול once its year has passed?

steps.title: Firstborn is linked to tithe, so lateness does not disqualify it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from a היקש between בכור and מעשר that a בכור is not disqualified when it is kept from one year to the next. This seems to make בן עזאי's פסוק unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall eat before ה׳ your God the tithe of your grain' and the rest of the verse. It links בכור to מעשר. Just as מעשר is not disqualified when it is kept from one year to the next, so too a בכור is not disqualified when it is kept from one year to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question: a late בכור is not פסול, because the תורה puts it side by side with מעשר. The גמרא is using this as a challenge, since it seems to show that a delay does not ruin a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both appear in the same פסוק, whatever is true of מעשר is true of בכור. מעשר does not spoil by waiting a year, so neither does בכור. If so, why does בן עזאי need his own פסוק to teach that a late offering is still accepted?

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
Compares two things that appear together in a פסוק (היקש)
A firstborn kosher animal, given to the כהן
Tithe
From one year to the next

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And you shall eat before the Lord your God
the tithe of your grain, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 14:23. The 'etc.' hides the key part: the same פסוק goes on to mention firstborns.

phrases.english: It juxtaposes a firstborn to tithe;
just as tithe is not disqualified
from one year to the next,
so too a firstborn is not disqualified
from one year to the next.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 1, and this answer is the point the גמרא uses as its challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for בן עזאי's פסוק teaching that a late offering is still accepted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The היקש of בכור to מעשר already shows that a delay does not disqualify. So a separate פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A firstborn does not atone, so other offerings needed their own source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we still need בן עזאי's פסוק. A בכור does not bring הרצאה, but other קדשים do, and we might have thought that a late offering of that kind would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought that this only applies to a בכור, which does not bring הרצאה. But קדשים that do bring הרצאה, say that they would not bring הרצאה when they are late. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בן עזאי. It explains why the בכור source is not enough to cover all קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is only a gift to the כהן and does not bring הרצאה, so lateness costs it nothing. Other קרבנות are meant to bring הרצאה, and we might have thought that being late stops them from working. בן עזאי's פסוק teaches that even these still work.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
You might have thought
Acceptance or atonement that a קרבן brings
They would bring acceptance or atonement
It teaches us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור is different from other קרבנות because it does not bring הרצאה. So a rule learned from בכור does not automatically apply to קרבנות that bring הרצאה.

phrases.english: It was necessary;
phrases.notes: He means בן עזאי's פסוק is still needed.

phrases.english: it might enter your mind to say:
this matter applies only to a firstborn,
which is not something that brings acceptance;
but sacrificial animals, which are for acceptance,
say they would not effect acceptance;
therefore it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by showing how בכור is different from other קדשים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the בכור source does not cover offerings that bring הרצאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the פסוק, we might have thought that late קרבנות which bring הרצאה would not bring it.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן עזאי's פסוק teaches that even קרבנות which bring הרצאה still work when they are brought late.

steps.title: Another source already teaches that delay does not ruin the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the rule is already known from 'והיה בך חטא', meaning the sin is on you and not on your קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, isn't this learned from there? 'And it will be sin in you', meaning there is sin in you, but there is no sin in your offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to בן עזאי. Another פסוק already seems to teach that a late קרבן is not ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about delaying a נדר says the person who delays has sinned. The גמרא reads it narrowly: the sin falls on the person, not on the קרבן. This covers all קרבנות, including those that bring הרצאה, so the answer in step 3 no longer saves בן עזאי.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
It is learned from there, from another source
Sin
Your offering

phrases.english: But still, isn't it derived from there?!
"And it will be sin in you"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:22, the פסוק about not delaying what you vowed.

phrases.english: but there is no sin in your offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new challenge after the answer in step 3, from a source that covers all קרבנות and not only בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for בן עזאי's פסוק, even after the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'והיה בך חטא' puts the sin of delay on the person and not on the קרבן. So no offering is ruined by lateness, and בן עזאי's פסוק again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: בן עזאי needs the פסוק to teach that the wife is not punished
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי cannot learn the late-קרבן rule from ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״, because he needs those words to teach that the sin of בל תאחר is on the man and not on his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן עזאי needs that פסוק for another lesson: ״and it will be a sin in you״, meaning in you and not in your wife. You might have thought that since רבי אלעזר (some say רבי יוחנן) said a man's wife dies only when people ask him for money and he does not have it, as it says, ״If you have nothing to pay, why should he take your bed from under you?״, then his wife would also die for the sin of בל תאחר. So the פסוק teaches us that she does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4. בן עזאי cannot use ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ for the קרבן rule, because those words are needed for a different lesson about the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ already shows that the קרבן itself is not ruined, so בן עזאי's own פסוק would not be needed. The answer is that ״בְךָ״ (in you) is needed to exclude the wife. Without it, we might have connected late vows with רבי אלעזר's teaching that a wife can die because of her husband's unpaid debts, since a vow is also a kind of unpaid debt.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it will be a sin in you", from the פסוק about delaying a vow
You might have thought to say (it introduces a mistaken first idea)
The prohibition against delaying a vow or a promised קרבן
It comes to teach us (this is why the פסוק is needed)

steps.confusionAlert: The words about the wife dying are not the הלכה the פסוק teaches. They are the mistaken first idea that the פסוק comes to reject.

phrases.english: And בן עזאי – he needs that for something else:
phrases.notes: "That" means the words ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ from step 4.

phrases.english: "And it will be a sin in you" – and not a sin in your wife.
It could have entered your mind to say:
Since רבי אלעזר said,
and some say it was רבי יוחנן:
A man's wife does not die

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מְבַקְּשִׁין מִמֶּנּוּ מָמוֹן וְאֵין לוֹ,
phrases.english: unless people ask him for money and he does not have it,
as it says: "If you have nothing to pay,
why should he take your bed from under you?" –
phrases.notes: משלי 22:27. "Your bed" is read here as hinting at your wife.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהַאי עָוֹן דְּ״בַל תְּאַחֵר״ נָמֵי מֵתָה;
phrases.english: then for this sin of "do not delay" she should also die;
so the פסוק teaches us that she does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by showing that ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ is already used for a different lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for another teaching (מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of רבי אלעזר's teaching about unpaid debts, we might have thought a man's wife dies for his sin of בל תאחר.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בְךָ״ limits the sin to the man himself. So בן עזאי's own פסוק is still needed to teach that a late קרבן is not ruined.
steps.whatToRemember: The words ״וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא״ are needed to teach that the punishment falls on the man and not on his wife. That is why בן עזאי still needs his own source for the late-קרבן rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long defense of בן עזאי that began in step 2. Every פסוק he uses now has its own job.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the view of אחרים in the ברייתא, who read ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ as being about wrong thoughts. Then it asks what רבי אליעזר, who has a different source, does with those words.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: the קרבן is ruined by a thought, and it is not ruined by eating on the third day. And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with the words ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the ברייתא. It quotes אחרים as background and asks what רבי אליעזר learns from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים use ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ to teach that פיגול comes from a wrong thought at the time of the עבודה, not from actually eating on the third day. רבי אליעזר learns that rule from a different source. So the גמרא asks what lesson he takes from these words, since every word of the תורה should teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others", a name for a תנא whose view is quoted in a ברייתא
A wrong thought or intention during the עבודה of a קרבן
"It shall not be counted", from the פסוק about פיגול
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from this פסוק?)

phrases.english: אחרים say:
It is ruined by a wrong thought,
and it is not ruined by eating it on the third day.
And רבי אליעזר –
what does he do with "it shall not be counted"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בן עזאי discussion and opens a new question about another line of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי אליעזר learns from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״, since he does not use it the way אחרים do.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: one wrong thought can cancel another
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ for רבי ינאי's teaching: a קרבן becomes פיגול only if no other wrong thought is mixed in with the פיגול thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי ינאי, who said: Where do we learn that thoughts push each other out? As it says ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״: he must not mix other thoughts into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 6. רבי אליעזר uses ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ to teach רבי ינאי's rule about mixed thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן becomes פיגול only when the כהן has a pure "eat it too late" thought. If he also mixes in a different wrong thought, such as eating it outside its place, the thoughts cancel each other and it is not פיגול. רבי ינאי hears this in the word ״יֵחָשֵׁב״, which is connected to מַחְשָׁבוֹת (thoughts).

keyTerms.meaning: Thoughts that push each other out (one wrong thought cancels the effect of another)
He must not mix in
A קרבן ruined by a thought of eating it after its proper time
From where do we learn it? (asking for the source)

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of רבי ינאי –
for רבי ינאי said:
From where do we learn that thoughts push each other out?
phrases.notes: He means an extra wrong thought stops the קרבן from becoming פיגול.

phrases.english: As it says: "It shall not be counted" –
he must not mix other thoughts into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר learns from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ that פיגול happens only when no other wrong thought is mixed in, because the thoughts cancel each other.

steps.title: רב מרי's version: one who has a wrong thought gets מלקות
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי reports רבי ינאי's teaching differently: ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ is a prohibition, so a person who has a wrong thought about קדשים gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מרי teaches it this way: רבי ינאי said, where do we learn that one who has a wrong thought about קדשים gets lashes? The פסוק says ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבי ינאי learned from ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״. This is another possible answer to the question about רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ is read as a command, "do not think", and not only as a statement about the קרבן. That makes it a לאו, so a כהן who has a wrong thought during the עבודה gets מלקות. רבי אליעזר still has a use for the words, just a different one from the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it (reports the teaching in this wording)
One who has a wrong thought while doing the עבודה of קדשים
Gets lashes (מלקות) for breaking a prohibition
The פסוק comes to teach (introduces the source)

steps.whatToRemember: ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ teaches something for רבי אליעזר in both versions. In the first version, other wrong thoughts cancel פיגול. In רב מרי's version, a person who has a wrong thought about קדשים gets מלקות.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב מָרִי מַתְנֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: And רב מרי teaches it this way: רבי ינאי said:
From where do we learn that one who has a wrong thought about קדשים gets lashes?
The פסוק teaches: "It shall not be counted."
phrases.notes: Here the words are read as a command: "do not think" such a thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב מָרִי מַתְנֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי ינאי's teaching. It is another way to answer the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ is a לאו, so a person who has a wrong thought about קדשים gets מלקות.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: a thought has no action, so how can it bring lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב מרי's version of רבי ינאי's teaching. A wrong thought is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and normally one does not get מלקות for such a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב מרי: A wrong thought is a prohibition that involves no action. For any prohibition that involves no action, a person does not get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the teaching from Step 8, which said a person gets מלקות for a wrong thought about קדשים. He points out that thinking is not an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that a לאו done without any physical action does not bring מלקות. A wrong thought about a קרבן is pure thinking, with no action. So רב מרי's version of רבי ינאי seems to break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah prohibition (a 'do not' command)
A prohibition broken without doing any physical action
One does not get lashes (מלקות) for it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Mari:
It is a prohibition that has no action in it,
phrases.notes: He means the wrong thought about the קרבן from Step 8. Thinking alone is not doing anything.

phrases.english: and any prohibition that has no action in it —
one does not get lashes for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מרי's version of רבי ינאי from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a person gets מלקות for a wrong thought about קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A thought is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and the general rule is that such a לאו does not bring מלקות

steps.title: רב מרי answers: this follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי answers that רבי ינאי's teaching follows רבי יהודה, who holds that one does get מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said to him: This follows רבי יהודה, who says that a person does get lashes for a prohibition that involves no action.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי defends his version. He explains that it fits the opinion of רבי יהודה, who disagrees with the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a לאו with no action brings no מלקות is not accepted by everyone. רבי יהודה holds that even such a לאו brings מלקות. So רבי ינאי's teaching is valid, but only according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is...': this teaching follows the opinion of a certain תנא
One does get lashes for it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב מרי, רבי ינאי reads ״לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב״ as a לאו that brings מלקות. This only works with רבי יהודה's view that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings מלקות.

phrases.english: He said to him: It follows Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: a prohibition that has no action in it —
one does get lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the teaching to a specific תנא who rejects the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that a לאו שאין בו מעשה brings no מלקות, so a thought cannot bring lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds that a לאו שאין בו מעשה does bring מלקות, and רבי ינאי's teaching follows him

steps.title: The משנה's general rule: place-thoughts make it invalid, time-thoughts make it פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the general rule. A wrong thought during any of the four blood services about a כזית outside its place makes the קרבן פסול, with no כרת. A thought about doing so beyond its time makes it פיגול, with כרת, provided the מתיר was offered כמצותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule. Anyone who slaughters, receives the blood, carries it, or throws it may intend to eat something that is normally eaten, or to burn something that is normally burned on the altar, in the amount of an olive. If he intends this outside its proper place, the offering is invalid but there is no כרת. If he intends this beyond its proper time, it is פיגול and one is liable for כרת, provided the permitting part was offered properly.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sums up the whole topic of wrong thoughts in one rule and adds an important condition for פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two kinds of wrong thought. A place-thought makes the קרבן פסול but never brings כרת. A time-thought makes it פיגול, and eating it brings כרת. The new condition is that פיגול only happens if the מתיר, the blood service that permits the meat, was otherwise done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text the גמרא discusses)
An olive's amount, the smallest amount that counts
Outside its proper place: a thought that makes the קרבן פסול
Beyond its proper time: a thought that makes the קרבן פיגול
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול
The 'permitter': the blood service that makes the קרבן's meat allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: The condition that the מתיר be offered כמצותו is the same idea as רבי ינאי's teaching in Step 7. A פיגול thought only works if no other wrong thought is mixed in.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: This is the general rule:
anyone who slaughters, or who receives the blood,
or who carries the blood, or who throws it,
intending to eat something that is normally eaten,
or to burn something that is normally burned on the altar,
in an olive's amount: if outside its place —
it is invalid, but there is no כרת for it.
If beyond its time, it is פיגול,
and one is liable for כרת for it,
provided he offers the permitter properly.
phrases.notes: The 'permitter' is the blood service. Offering it 'properly' here means with no wrong thought except the time-thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the גמרא's discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A place-thought makes the קרבן פסול with no כרת. A time-thought makes it פיגול with כרת, but only if the מתיר was offered כמצותו.

steps.title: Examples of the permitter offered properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three cases where the מתיר is offered כמצותו. In each case the only wrong thought is a time-thought, while the other services are done in silence.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the permitter offered properly? He slaughtered in silence, and received, carried, and threw the blood with a beyond-its-time thought. Or he slaughtered with a beyond-its-time thought, and received, carried, and threw in silence. Or he did all four services with a beyond-its-time thought. These are cases where the permitter is offered properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its own condition from Step 11 by giving clear examples of the מתיר being offered כמצותו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Properly' does not mean with no wrong thought at all, since there is a time-thought in every case. It means that the only wrong thought is the time-thought. Services done בשתיקה, with no thought at all, do not spoil the פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: How? (introduces examples)
In silence, with no special thought at all
Properly, according to its מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'offered properly' means the קרבן is kosher. Here it means only that no thought other than the פיגול time-thought was mixed in, so the פיגול takes full effect.

phrases.english: How is the permitter offered properly?
He slaughtered in silence,
and received, carried, and threw the blood with a beyond-its-time thought;
or he slaughtered with a beyond-its-time thought,
and received, carried, and threw in silence;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ –
phrases.english: or he slaughtered, received, carried, and threw, all with a beyond-its-time thought —
this is where he offers the permitter properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the condition stated at the end of Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מתיר is offered כמצותו when the only wrong thought in the services is a time-thought, even if other services were done בשתיקה.

steps.title: Examples of the permitter not offered properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives cases where the מתיר is not offered כמצותו, because a place-thought was mixed in with the time-thought. In these cases the קרבן is only פסול, not פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is the permitter not offered properly? He slaughtered with an outside-its-place thought, and received, carried, and threw with a beyond-its-time thought. Or he slaughtered with a beyond-its-time thought, and received, carried, and threw with an outside-its-place thought. Or he did all four services with an outside-its-place thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite examples: cases where a place-thought spoils things, so the time-thought does not create פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a place-thought enters any service, the מתיר was not offered כמצותו. So even if there was also a time-thought, there is no פיגול and no כרת, and the קרבן is just פסול. In this unnamed view, the order of the thoughts does not matter. רבי יהודה disagrees in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Was not offered properly, because a different wrong thought was mixed in
He slaughtered (the first of the four services)
He threw the blood on the altar (the last of the four services)

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול needs a 'clean' time-thought. If a place-thought is mixed into any of the four services, the קרבן is only פסול, with no כרת. This matches רבי ינאי's teaching in Step 7.

phrases.english: How is the permitter not offered properly?
He slaughtered with an outside-its-place thought,
and received, carried, and threw with a beyond-its-time thought;
or he slaughtered with a beyond-its-time thought,
and received, carried, and threw with an outside-its-place thought;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ (וְלִזְמַנּוֹ).
phrases.english: or he slaughtered, received, carried, and threw, all with an outside-its-place thought.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets, 'and its time', is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected text leaves it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite cases to Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a place-thought is mixed into any of the services, the מתיר was not offered כמצותו, so there is no פיגול and the קרבן is just פסול.

steps.title: A פסח or חטאת with a not-for-its-sake thought mixed in
steps.stepSummary: With a פסח or חטאת, a שלא לשמן thought mixed together with a time-thought also means the מתיר was not offered כמצותו, so there is no פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח or חטאת that was slaughtered not for its sake, and then the blood was collected, carried and sprinkled with a thought beyond its time. Or it was slaughtered with a time-thought, and the other services were done not for its sake. Or all the services, through the sprinkling, were done not for its sake. In all of these the מתיר was not offered כמצותו.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more cases to its list of 'the מתיר was not offered כמצותו.' This time the extra wrong thought is שלא לשמן, not a place-thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח and a חטאת become פסול when they are offered שלא לשמן, so for them that thought is a real disqualifying thought, just like a place-thought. Because a disqualifying thought spoiled the services, the time-thought cannot make the קרבן פיגול. The order does not matter here: whether the שלא לשמן thought comes first or second, the result is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake: having in mind a different kind of קרבן
The קרבן פסח, offered on ערב פסח
A sin offering
And he carried (the blood to the מזבח), one of the four blood services

phrases.english: The פסח and the חטאת that one slaughtered not for their sake,
and he collected, carried and sprinkled with a thought beyond its time;
phrases.notes: 'Beyond its time' means he planned to eat or burn it after the time the תורה allows.

phrases.english: or that one slaughtered with a thought beyond its time,
and collected, carried and sprinkled not for their sake;
or that one slaughtered, collected, carried
and sprinkled their blood not for their sake –
this is a case where the permitting part was not offered according to its rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues Step 13's list of cases where the מתיר is not offered כמצותו, swapping the place-thought for a שלא לשמן thought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a פסח or חטאת, a שלא לשמן thought anywhere alongside the time-thought means the מתיר was not offered כמצותו, so it is not פיגול.

steps.title: Thoughts of eating both outside its place and beyond its time
steps.stepSummary: If he planned to eat some of the meat outside its place and some after its time, the קרבן is only פסול, without כרת, whatever the order and even with half-כזית amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did a service planning to eat a כזית outside and a כזית tomorrow, or a כזית tomorrow and a כזית outside, or half a כזית outside and half a כזית tomorrow, or half a כזית tomorrow and half a כזית outside, the קרבן is פסול, and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now looks at a case where he has both a place-thought and a time-thought, in either order. It rules that the קרבן is only פסול, not פיגול. Whether these thoughts are in one service or in two is argued in steps 18-20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a place-thought is mixed in, the time-thought cannot create פיגול, so the order of the two thoughts does not matter. The half-כזית cases show that the two halves join to make a full כזית that disqualifies. Still, there is no כרת, because neither thought alone reaches a full כזית of time-thought.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the smallest amount that counts for these thoughts
Half an olive-bulk
Outside (the place where it may be eaten)
Tomorrow (after the time it may be eaten)
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up פסול and פיגול. Both mean the קרבן cannot be eaten, but only פיגול carries כרת for someone who eats it.

phrases.english: To eat an olive-bulk outside and an olive-bulk tomorrow;
an olive-bulk tomorrow and an olive-bulk outside;

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר;
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk outside and half an olive-bulk tomorrow;

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk tomorrow and half an olive-bulk outside –
it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with cases that combine a place-thought and a time-thought, now listing both orders and half-כזית amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A place-thought mixed with a time-thought, in either order and even in half-כזית amounts, makes the קרבן פסול without כרת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the first thought decides; חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the time-thought came first it is פיגול with כרת, and if the place-thought came first it is only פסול. חכמים say both cases are only פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said, this is the rule: whenever the time-thought came before the place-thought, it is פיגול and there is כרת. If the place-thought came before the time-thought, it is פסול and there is no כרת. חכמים say: in both cases it is פסול, and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the ruling in Step 15 and says the order of the thoughts matters. חכמים stick with the first view: it is always only פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's view, once the time-thought comes first it has already done its work and made the קרבן פיגול, and a later place-thought cannot undo that. If the place-thought comes first, it spoils the קרבן before the time-thought shows up, so the result is only פסול. חכמים hold that any mixing of the two thoughts keeps it from being פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
A thought about doing it beyond its time
A thought about doing it outside its place
Came first, preceded
A קרבן ruined by a time-thought, with כרת for eating it
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is exactly what the גמרא now goes on to analyze: when does the order of the thoughts make a difference?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said, this is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁמַּחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: any case where the thought about time came before the thought about place –
it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן –
phrases.english: And if the thought about place came before the thought about time –
it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה – פָּסוּל, וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: in both this case and that case, it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה disagrees with Step 15's ruling, and חכמים support it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the earlier thought decides (time first means פיגול with כרת, place first means פסול only). חכמים: always פסול without כרת.

steps.title: Eating and burning do not join together
steps.stepSummary: A wrong thought to eat half a כזית and to burn half a כזית does not add up to a full כזית, so the קרבן stays כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he planned to eat half a כזית and to burn half a כזית (at the wrong time or place), the קרבן is כשר, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one last case. Two half-amounts of different kinds of thoughts, one for eating and one for burning on the מזבח, do not combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, two halves did join, because both were about eating. Here one half is about eating, which is done by people, and the other is about burning, which is done on the מזבח. Since these are different kinds of use, they cannot add up to a full כזית, and nothing disqualifies the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning on the מזבח
Eating
Join together to make up a full amount
Fit, valid

steps.whatToRemember: Mixed thoughts can make a קרבן פסול or block פיגול, but half-amounts only add up when they are the same kind of use. Eating plus burning does not add up.

phrases.english: To eat half an olive-bulk
and to burn half an olive-bulk – it is fit;
because eating and burning do not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶאֱכוֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the joining of half-amounts from Step 15: they join only when they are the same kind of use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a כזית for eating and half a כזית for burning do not combine, so the קרבן is כשר.

steps.title: אילפא: the dispute is only across two services
steps.stepSummary: אילפא says רבי יהודה and חכמים argue only when the two thoughts were in two different services. In one service, everyone agrees it counts as mixed thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אילפא said, the מחלוקת is when the thoughts were in two services. But in one service, everyone agrees it counts as a mixing of thoughts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking how far the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and חכמים reaches. אילפא limits it to thoughts held in two separate services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אילפא, רבי יהודה says the first thought decides only when each thought belongs to its own service, for example time during the slaughtering and place during the sprinkling. If both thoughts come up within one service, even רבי יהודה treats them as one mixed thought. So it is only פסול, not פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate services
One single service
Everyone agrees
A mixing of thoughts, which blocks פיגול

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ilfa says:
the disagreement is with regard to two services;
phrases.notes: He means the argument of רבי יהודה and חכמים from the משנה.

phrases.english: but in one service –
all agree it is a mixing of thoughts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by defining which cases the מחלוקת in Step 16 covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's 'first thought decides' applies only across two services. Within one service, all agree it is a mixing of thoughts, so it is פסול only.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute applies even in one service
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with אילפא and says רבי יהודה's rule applies even when both thoughts were in one service.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: even in one service there is the מחלוקת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different view from אילפא. For him, רבי יהודה and חכמים argue even when both thoughts were in the same service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, even within a single service the order of the thoughts counts. If the time-thought was said first, רבי יהודה rules פיגול, while חכמים still say it is only פסול. The next step asks how this fits the structure of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
even in one service there is a disagreement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אילפא in Step 18 by widening the מחלוקת to a single service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when both thoughts are in one service, רבי יהודה and חכמים argue, and for רבי יהודה the first thought decides.

steps.title: The first and last parts of the משנה should match, which fits אילפא but not רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the first part of the משנה talks about two services, so the last part should too. That fits אילפא, but it seems odd for רבי יוחנן, who reads the last part as talking about one service.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to אילפא: the first part of the משנה is about two services, so the last part is also about two services. But according to רבי יוחנן, would the first part be about two services and the last part about only one service?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. It says the two halves of the משנה should be about the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה clearly describes wrong thoughts spread over two separate services. אילפא reads the last part the same way, so the משנה is consistent. רבי יוחנן applies the last part even to one service, which seems to break that pattern, so the גמרא asks how he can split the משנה like that.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (used to set one view up against another that seems harder)
The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה
A service in bringing a קרבן, like slaughtering, collecting the blood, carrying it, or throwing it

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about what the הלכה is in each case. It is about how to read the משנה: the גמרא expects its first and last parts to describe the same kind of case, two services.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ilfa,
since the first part is about two services,
phrases.notes: The first part is the case where he slaughtered with no special thought and then had a wrong thought while collecting or throwing the blood.

phrases.english: the last part is also about two services.
But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
the first part is about two services,
and the last part is about one service?!
phrases.notes: The last part is where רבי יהודה and חכמים argue over which wrong thought came first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the argument between אילפא (step 18) and רבי יוחנן (step 19) against how the משנה is built.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that רבי יהודה's rule applies even within one service.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first and last parts of a משנה should describe the same kind of case. The first part is clearly about two services, so the last part should be too. רבי יוחנן's reading makes the two parts uneven.
